caseno: Appeal from original decree No. 233 (Probate) of 1970.
lawyer:
M.A. Rouf ----- For the Appellant.
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Md Shafiqur Rahman ----- For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Mohd. Mazibar Rahman Mia ----- Petitioner- Appellant. 
Vs.
Naresh Chandra Guha ----- Principal opposite party.
full_judgment:
M H. Rahman, J-This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 30-6-70 passed by Mr. Aminullah Khan, District Judge, Barisal in Misc. Case No. 4 of 1970 arising out of probate case No. 17 of 1968 there. 

 4. On 1-6-79 respondent No. 1 filed an application for hearing of the question of maintainability of the application and for proving the locus standi of the petitioner. After hearing both the parties the learned District Judge by his order dated the 30th June, 1970 dismissed the Miscellaneous case after holding that the petitioner had no interest in the estate of the deceased and as such he had no locus standi to pray for revocation of the probate. In rejecting the application of the petitioner the learned District Judge also considered that the property of the deceased had not been attached and in the money suit filed by the petitioner proper security had been given for realisation of the loan. 

 5. Mr. M.A. Rouf, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, has only submitted two grounds; that the learned District Judge illegally held that the petitioner had no locus standi to file an application for revocation of the probate, and that the maintainability of such an application ought not to have been rejected summarily without giving opportunity to the petitioner for adducing evidence in the matter. In support of his contention that the creditor who alleges fraud has got locus standi to file an application for revocation of a probate he has cited to us the case of Sarala Sundari vs. Dina Bandhu Roy, AIR 1944 (PC) 11. 

 6. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 1 has submitted that only those persons who could be cited before the grant of probate are the persons who could apply to revoke the probate. In this case the creditor has no interest in the properly of the deceased and as he could not be cited before the grant of probate he had no locus standi to pray for revocation of the probate. He has cited the case of Md. Abdul Jalil vs. Surendra Nath in 21 DLR 331. He has also pointed out that the facts in the present case are distinguishable from the facts reported in the case cited by the learned Advocate for the Appellant. 

 7. The reported case of M.A. Jalil Surendra Nath has got no relevance in this case. In that case the provisions of sec. 283 of the Succession Act, 1925 were construed for determining the question as to who could be parties to a proceeding for probate. Clause (c) of subsection (1) of section 283 clearly provides for issuance of citations for calling upon all persons claiming any interest in the estate of the deceased to come and see the proceeding before the grant of probate. 

 "(a) the proceeding to obtain the grant were defective in substance, or (b) the grant was obtained fraudulently by making a false suggestion or by concealing from the court something material to the cause; or (c) the grant was obtained by means of an untrue allegation of a fact essential in point of law to justify the grant, though such allegation was made in ignorance or inadvertently; (d) the grant has become useless and inoperative through circumstances; or (e) the person to whom the grant was made has wilfully and without reasonable cause omitted to, exhibit an inventory or account in accordance with the provisions of chapter VII of this part, or has exhibited under that chapter an inventory or account which is untrue in a material respect." In the aforesaid case of Sarala Sundari vs. Dinabandhu Roy the suggestion that it is only these persons who could be cited before the grant of probate who are the persons who could apply to revoke the probate has been repelled as that would put the meaning of "just causes" as explained in section 263 on too narrow a footing. It has been observed in this case that :— "If a person is complaining that he has in fact been defrauded, he is one of the persons who is injured by fraud alleged and that person is entitled to have his redress by applying to revoke the probate and thereby cause the fraud to become inoperative. If he had not such a right as that it is very difficult to know what right a creditor in those circumstances or a person injured by the fraud, could have, otherwise the probate would stand and he would be affected by the probate which had been obtained exhypothesi fraudulently." 

 9. A creditor-simpliciter cannot be said so have a locus standi to pray for revocation of the probate for it would be the duty of whoever is the grantee to pay debts first, and his interest cannot be affected by any dispossession made by the deceased. But when it is alleged by a creditor that the grant was obtained by means of untrue allegation or by making false suggestion or by concealing from the court something material to the case and when such fraudulent suggestion or concealment would put the creditor in jeopardy such creditor would be entitled to ask for revocation of a probate. 

 10. In the case of Sarala Sundari vs. Dinabandhu Roy, the testator Haralal Saha died in 1927. Sons of the deceased were in financial difficulties. In November, 1933 the creditor firm obtained a money decree against the sons who were later on declared insolvent. In the meantime in 1933 the widow of Haralal Saha applied for probate. The probate granted to her attracted a good deal of suspicions and the creditor filed an application for revocation in August, 1935 for probate and in the facts and circumstances of the case it was held that the creditor and locus standi to ask for revocation of the probate. In the instant case the Will was executed on 9th December, 1963 and the testator died on 16-3-68 and within a month an application for probate was filed and the probate was granted on 28th April, 1969. The creditor claimed to have advanced loans in between 25-3-65 to 4-1-67. The creditor had also filed a suit against the heirs of the deceased and in obedience to the order of the Court the heirs of the deceased furnished security for the alleged claim. In the facts and circumstances of the case it cannot be said said that the Will was executed to defraud the creditor or if the probate was allowed to stand the creditor would suffer any injury for the alleged fraudulent execution of the Will. In the background of the case, the learned District Judge has rightly held that the appellant petitioner had no locus standi to pray for revocation of the probate. The other objection that the learned District Judge acted illegally in rejecting the application of the petitioner summarily without giving any opportunity to adduce evidence has got no substance. It is the duty of the court to examine an application and to ascertain the facts whether any cause of action has been revealed before it decides to proceed with the matter. The learned District Judge, on consideration of the facts not disputed in the pleadings of the parties, found that the petitioner had no locus standi and rejected the application on the ground of maintainability. We do not find any reasons to interfere with the impugned order.
